explanation: Variadic templates are a feature introduced in C++11 that allow templates to accept an arbitrary number of template parameters, including types and non-type values. They enable writing highly flexible and generic code, such as tuple implementations, parameter forwarding, and compile-time computations. Variadic templates are fundamental for modern C++ metaprogramming, facilitating code reuse and type safety without resorting to preprocessor macros.
example_explanation: This example defines a variadic template class 'MyTuple' that can hold an arbitrary number of elements of different types. It uses a parameter pack 'Types...' to accept multiple type parameters, demonstrating how variadic templates enable flexible, type-safe data structures. The 'print' method utilizes index sequences and fold expressions (C++17) to iterate over and output each element, showcasing modern C++ idioms for working with parameter packs. The main function creates an instance with three different types and prints their values, illustrating the power and convenience of variadic templates in generic programming.
